requirements.text: Creates or edits workflows under .github/workflows/ with valid events, jobs, and context use, and runs actionlint on changed files when available.
Pins every third-party uses: reference to a full 40-character SHA with an adjacent release comment.
Declares explicit permissions at workflow or job scope and never uses write-all.
Validates workflow_dispatch and workflow_call inputs before shell or deploy steps, and passes expression values through env: instead of inline run: interpolation.
Declares shell: bash on every composite run: step (not on uses: steps), starts shell blocks with set -euo pipefail, and forwards inputs through env:.
Maps caller-visible outputs from $GITHUB_OUTPUT, documents them, and treats a changed input or output contract as a versioning event.
Chooses inline steps, a script, a reusable workflow, or a composite action by the unit of reuse and states the reason.
Diagnoses a failed run from the first failed step with log evidence before proposing a fix.
States that pull_request_target runs the default-branch workflow definition, so a workflow fix inside a PR does not change that PR's run.
When an action option needs a wider GITHUB_TOKEN scope, grants that scope explicitly or disables the option.
When invoked by internal-review-code, returns only the contributor record fields and no verdict, severity, or merge decision.
Routes runner-fleet health, rulesets, and organization Actions policy to internal-github-platform.

cases.prompt: Harden this release workflow before we enable it.
cases.initial_state: The defective workflow fixture is the target file.
cases.expected_output: A corrected workflow with SHA-pinned actions, least-privilege permissions, and an actionlint step in the validation notes.

assertions.text: Output YAML has every third-party uses: at a 40-character SHA and no write-all; actionlint passes on it.
Each pin has an adjacent release comment.
Permissions name only the scopes the release job needs.

cases.prompt: Fix this composite action so it is safe and exposes the Terraform version as an output.
cases.initial_state: The defective composite action fixture is the target action.yml.
cases.expected_output: A corrected action.yml with env-forwarded inputs, bash strict mode, input validation, and an output mapped from $GITHUB_OUTPUT.

assertions.text: Output action.yml has no ${{ inputs.* }} inside run:, and every run: step declares shell: bash.
The output is written to $GITHUB_OUTPUT and mapped under outputs.
The version input is validated before download.

forbidden_actions: Add shell: to a uses: step.

cases.prompt: I fixed this pull_request_target workflow in my PR but re-running the check still fails. Why?
cases.initial_state: The PR modifies the pull_request_target workflow fixture.
cases.expected_output: An explanation that the run uses the default-branch definition and the fix takes effect after merge.

assertions.text: Answer states that the PR run keeps using the default-branch definition until merge.
Suggests validating the change after merge or on a fork-safe trigger.

forbidden_actions: Claim that re-running the PR check will pick up the edit.

cases.prompt: Run 9912 failed; find the cause and fix it.
cases.initial_state: The failed-run log fixture is the only evidence.
cases.expected_output: A diagnosis citing the Report coverage step and a fix that grants pull-requests: write or disables the comment option.

assertions.text: Diagnosis cites the failing step's log line and either grants the named scope or disables the option.
States that later steps were skipped, not failed.

cases.prompt: Make this manual deploy workflow safe to run.
cases.initial_state: The dispatch workflow fixture is the target file.
cases.expected_output: A workflow that restricts the environment input and passes it through env: to the script.

assertions.text: Output validates the input against an allowlist before any shell or deploy step uses it.
Uses a choice input or an explicit allowlist check.

cases.prompt: Three workflows repeat the same build, test, and publish jobs with different runners. How should we share them?
cases.expected_output: A reuse recommendation with the reason tied to the unit of reuse.

assertions.text: The chosen pattern matches the unit of reuse.
States what would change the choice.

pass: Recommends a reusable workflow because jobs, runners, and permissions are shared.
fail: Recommends a composite action for job-level orchestration.

cases.prompt: Envelope: role domain-routing, parent internal-review-code, deliverable GitHub Actions contributor observations, evidence a diff adding a workflow step.
cases.initial_state: internal-review-code invokes the skill as a contributor.
cases.expected_output: One contributor record with the declared fields only.

assertions.text: Output has exactly the contributor record fields and no verdict or severity.

pass: Returns domain, changed_contract_surfaces, observations, probes, applicable_validations, compatibility_risks, and evidence_gaps only.
fail: Adds a verdict, severity, or merge recommendation.

cases.prompt: Jobs across the org wait 20 minutes for our self-hosted runners. Fix it.
cases.expected_output: A handoff to internal-github-platform with the evidence needed.

assertions.text: Output routes to internal-github-platform and does not edit workflow YAML.

pass: Names internal-github-platform as owner and lists queue-time evidence to collect.
fail: Edits runs-on labels in workflows as the fix.
